algorithm.title: Failure to Thrive (FTT): Diagnosis. (Ultimately, Consider All Potential Causes of FTT in Each Patient, as Etiology Is Often Multifactorial.)

cell.label: Measure and plot weight, length, and head circumference. Is poor growth symmetric, or is the head circumference spared (asymmetric)?
Suggests congenital or metabolic causes. Are GI symptoms present (diarrhea, steatorrhea, abdominal pain)?
Consider malabsorption: cow's milk protein allergy, cystic fibrosis, celiac disease, biliary atresia, inflammatory bowel disease, disaccharidase deficiency, or chronic diarrhea present?
Consider sweat test, tissue transglutaminase (TTG), gamma-glutaryl transferase (GGT), specialist referral.
Likely cause of FTT. Confirm diagnosis and treat as indicated.

Look for signs of chronic disease, which could be leading to increased metabolic needs: prematurity, recurrent infections, cardiac or pulmonary disorders, malignancy, renal or liver disease, or hyperthyroidism (including laboratory testing if indicated). Chronic disease present?
Consider improper utilization of calories: inborn errors of metabolism, storage disorders, or growth hormone deficiency. Consider specialist referral.
Suggests inadequate caloric intake. Observe feeding. Are there mechanical feeding difficulties?
Likely cause of FTT. Treat as indicated.

Investigate for psychosocial problems. Food diary to look for poor diet, inappropriate foods, unusual diets. Observed feedings to look for behavioral problems or oral aversion. In-depth interviews to look for parental mental health disorders, neglect, poverty, incorrect formula preparation.
